finding: the 18 MAPGEN-018 GCPs were a Cartesian product
detail: 6 meridian x-observations on the top border and 3 parallel y-observations on the left border were crossed into 18 rows. Each longitude reused one pixel_x three times and each latitude reused one pixel_y six times, so there were 9 primitive measurements, not 18 control points.
consequence: the fit/holdout split shared primitive observations (every held-out point's y came from a parallel also used in the fit), so the 60 m 'holdout RMS' measured how well an affine model reproduces a rectangle - which it does perfectly by construction - and said nothing about geographic accuracy.
second_finding: one independent check point could not reveal this. Berlin happened to land at 9.28 km, which looked like ordinary 18th-century placement error.
what_the_checks_show: 5 identified towns give median 9.3 km, p90 27.7 km, max 28.6 km. The windows predicted for Frankfurt an der Oder, Neuruppin and Schwedt contained Fuerstenwalde, Fehrbellin and Angermuende instead - a systematic error, not scatter.
action: georeference status downgraded to GEOREFERENCE_PROVISIONAL_RECONSTRUCTED_GRID; the 18 rows are retained as RECONSTRUCTED_GRID_POINT and counted as 0 production GCPs; no geometry, no control.
